title: Records of truth change only through the artifact door — one journaled machine, caller measured not claimed, a hand edit is a ruling not a write.
question: Ticket 481221f45884 stands at [PROVED] with no crossing in the harbor journal: its cursor was moved by hand (commit 42e3db0, 2026-09-10). 'Records go through their door' is a memory and a paragraph; 145 code sites in 69 files write record paths with write_text. Akien asked whether a Claude Code config filter could stop CC writing certain extensions, and then ruled the larger shape.
ruling: Akien, 2026-09-13, across one conversation — the three verbatim passages in the_ruling_verbatim, ending 'approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH'.
the_ruling_verbatim: if we are going to build that, i'd say we have to rename the files. .json could become .artifact for those classes of files. then we only disallow one extension. but the problem with stopping there is that then i'm on the hook for those edits. so we have to build a machine that you must use to update .artifacts and the job of the machine will be in part to assure that a hand edits only happen with an explicit from me to allow that. so our inspection process that we have now for all artifacts would ask me to approve it.

almost... this also means updates to every gate that touches such a thing. and i think the machine does an introspective call stack check and records who called it. the gates can trigger the mechanism (normal flow), command line (me), and you (how would you trigger it? how would it know to trust you? how far would it have to?)... what i'd really like a fingerprint like thing but i think this mechanism comes close enough? ... we might have to update skills too
good assessment. and this is the P0 we tackle first. well done sir. approved thru PROVED RULED BLESSED FROM ON HIGH
now_the_spec_says: A record of truth changes only through the artifact door, which journals WHO wrote it from the caller's cgroup ancestry; a change outside the door is refused at commit, and a hand edit is parked as a ruling for Akien — never written as truth.
what_the_rule_was_always_about: Law 7's second half — a record of truth never collapses an error — and Law 6's gate. A hand edit is a collapsed error: the record says something happened (a crossing, a seal, a clearance) that no gate performed. The rule was never 'CC may not edit JSON'; it was that the WHO of every change to a record is part of the record, and today the who is nowhere. The deny-rule Akien asked about would put HIM on the hook for every edit CC could not make, which is why the ruling grew into a machine: the door assures a hand edit happens only with his explicit approval through the existing inspection process.
the_distinction_that_now_governs: WHO is kernel truth; WHY is testimony. The caller's class (a gate under a cairn-*.service unit; CC under the superclaude scope; Akien at a login shell) is read from cgroup ancestry the caller cannot forge from inside; the call stack Akien asked for is journaled beside it as provenance — which gate, which line — and is never used to decide trust. A change whose sha is not the journal's last sha_after is refused at commit, whoever made it, Akien included; his escape route is the hand-edit verb, which parks the diff and opens a ruling he signs.
what_this_does_not_permit: It does not make the door an owner (Law 6: a tool has users). It does not license CC to skip the door for 'small' edits — there is no size below which a record write is not a record write. It does not retire the harbor journal: that records boats MOVING, this records bytes CHANGING, and their disagreement is a finding. It does not treat the pre-commit hook and the Claude Code deny rules as physics: they are policy a process can bypass, and the physics (record roots owned by a second unix user, the door the only sudo-relay path) is an IOU carried on the ticket.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — 'records go through their door' was prose)
Law 7 (a record of truth never collapses an error — a hand edit is one)
Law 6 (one owner gates writes; the door is the gate and the journal is who came through it)
Law 10 (the caller is measured from /proc, not asked)
Law 9 (his own commits are translations like any other artifact — the door refuses his hand edit too, and the ruling verb is his escape)
